messages.subject: Community Occupancy / Abundance models
parts:
Hello,
I am curious if any of you all have been using Nimble to fit community occupancy or abundance models? I've been working on some, but keep having the R session abort on me when I try to fit the model with covariates. I did have an error in my priors and initial values, but have resolved that. I'm still getting an issue related to the Yc , the counts array. As the model is compiled I see this: 

defining model...
Detected Yc as data within 'constants'.
Adding Yc as data for building model.
building model...
setting data and initial values...
running calculate on model (any error reports that follow may simply reflect missing values in model variables) ... 
checking model sizes and dimensions...
checking model calculations...
Infinite values were detected in model variable: logProb_Yc.
model building finished.
compiling... this may take a minute. Use 'showCompilerOutput = TRUE' to see C++ compilation details.

Any thoughts?

messages.author: dd632bd3bbcdd7e9
messages.subject: Re: Community Occupancy / Abundance models
parts:
Hi Ben,

Yes, people have been using nimble for multi-species occupancy and abundance models.  We have a paper led by Lauren Ponisio that will be coming out in Ecology & Evolution that includes such cases.  I'll point to the preprint when the journal posts it.  In the meantime, you could take a look at our workshop materials (https://github.com/nimble-training).  The workshop I gave at Vogelwarte might have the most relevant examples: https://github.com/nimble-training/nimble-Vogelwarte-workshop-2018

There might be two issues going on.  nimble should not crash your R session.  One guess it that your model code has declarations accessing elements of variables that don't exist, i.e. using indices that are too big.  (That still shouldn't crash your system, but conceivably it could.)

Separately, it looks like you need to debug initial values.  The message I sent on Jan. 24 on this thread (https://groups.google.com/forum/#!topic/nimble-users/9PmFGuJCrbg) suggests how to do that.  We should really get more guides like this more easily available to users.  Anyone want to contribute to the project by helping put something like that together?

Beyond that, we'd need to see a minimal reproducible example to figure out what's going on in your case.

HTH
-Perry
